issue_context.title: TryAddWithoutValidation works differently for HttpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders and HttpRequestMessage.Headers
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/ncl See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Description Header in `HttpClient.DefaultRequestHeaders` is formatted and sent as `en-US, en; q=0.5` (note the spaces). ```cs var client = new HttpClient(); var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, new Uri("http://localhost/")); client.DefaultRequestHeaders.TryAddWithoutValidation("Accept-Language", "en-US,en;q=0.5"); client.Send(request); ``` Header in `HttpRequestMessage.Headers` is untouched and sent as `en-US,en;q=0.5`. ```cs var client = new HttpClient(); var request = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, new Uri("http://localhost/")); request.Headers.TryAddWithoutValidation("Accept-Language", "en-US,en;q=0.5"); client.Send(request); ``` ### Configuration .NET 5
Author: AbeniMatteo
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Net.Http`, `untriaged`
Milestone: -

The code here:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/89fbdcafcc09af0e1c2d86783eb8e8b93a743968/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/Headers/HttpHeaders.cs#L557
is parsing the data from the default headers being added.  Looking back through history, it appears this was done when the handler would enumerate the headers in a way that would parse/validate them, in which case it was desirable to forcible do that parsing/validation just once for the default header collection rather than on every send.  But as of https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/pull/41640 in .NET 5, we're no longer doing that parsing/validation forcibly as part of actually sending the request, which means that up-front parsing/validation of the default header collection is now not only unnecessary work but also leads to the behavioral discrepancy highlighted in this issue.  Seems like we should just stop doing that.

> Seems like we should just stop doing that.

By "that", you mean:

> up-front parsing/validation of the default header collection

? Seems reasonable to me.
Triage: we should investigate here and if we parse the headers we should not.

This is getting interesting. 😄 
`DebuggerDisplayAttribute` works the opposite way. Now `HttpRequestMessage.Headers` is the one being formatted.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/634710/111203662-946aa280-85c5-11eb-9fc1-b86d034269e0.png)

> DebuggerDisplayAttribute works the opposite way

There's no DebuggerDisplayAttribute here: the debugger is just calling ToString().

I also don't see the behavior you're seeing... what .NET version is that?  ToString() shouldn't be parsing the values (and I don't see it doing so in the code).

The problem appears after hovering `.Headers` then `request` and again `.Headers`.
Apparently calling `request.ToString()` changes the value, you can also trigger it programmatically:
```cs
var a = request.Headers.ToString(); // Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.5
request.ToString();
var b = request.Headers.ToString(); // Accept-Language: en-US, en; q=0.5
```

I'm using .NET 5.0.201 with VS 2019 Version 16.9.1.

> Apparently calling request.ToString() changes the value

Yes.  I thought you were just looking at headers, but HttpRequestMessage.ToString() enumerates HttpHeaders (rather than using its ToString()), and such enumerating will parse.

review_comments:
Because it was wrong :)

It turns out we only ever hit AddHeaders code path for two things:
1) Adding in the DefaultRequestHeaders
2) Forwarding headers for a decompressed response in SocketsHttpHandler

For (2), the headers are all raw response headers, so in AddHeaders above, the `if (sourceValue is HeaderStoreItemInfo info)` check will always be false and we'll never hit this AddHeaderInfo path.

For (1), the headers are all forced to be in HeaderStoreItemInfo instances (something else to revisit), and we were only getting here after calling ParseRawHeaderValues, which for a custom header with no validation would basically transfer the raw value to the parsed field.

But I removed that ParseRawHeaderValues call, so now we may still have raw values here.
